title: I haven't spent a single dollar making this game.
author: FullLet2258
selftext:
As crazy as it might sound, I literally haven't spent a single cent making this game. Obviously, I've used a lot of AI, but most of the resources were free, and I mainly relied on DeepSeek.

And as much as it might look like Vampire Survivors, trust me when I say it's a completely different game. Of course, it's a roguelite where you kill mobs, choose abilities, and so on, but the actual gameplay is something entirely different.

I don't have a Steam page yet, but if you'd like, you can check out the UI here: [https://strikemeta.lat/soulprado](https://strikemeta.lat/soulprado)

replies.author: PM_Me_Those_
replies.body: For reference, lets say 4 hours a day of time over 6+ months is well over 700 hours of time. For reference that is around $21,000 if working on an 'average US wage'. OP spent SHITLOADS of money on this project.

replies.author: living_david_aloca
replies.body: Assuming that OP would have worked instead, which is not always in their control and if in a salaried position then the extra hours don’t directly equate to extra pay. Not everything is a time = money calculation.

replies.author: PM_Me_Those_
replies.body: Quite literally all things can be quantified this way. (at least all things that cost us time, we are not immortal).

replies.author: living_david_aloca
replies.body: You can literally price time as money but that doesn’t mean the time is worth that money. Time you would otherwise have spent watching Netflix is not priced the same way, or at all really, the way you’d price your working time.

replies.author: PM_Me_Those_
replies.body:
Yea it absolutely is and can be applied in the same way. 

ie; You are watching Netflix 700 hours a year, had you applied yourself during those hours thats a pretty big time/value loss, absolutely. 

Now, even the most productive people don't just work every waking minute and/or even make money every waking minute, but the point is you can still quantify it that way and people who do are probably better with money than people who don't. Generally speaking.

replies.author: living_david_aloca
replies.body: Time is not any more meaningful when judged in money terms. At any rate, OP didn’t spend money building the game if they would not have otherwise made money using their time.

replies.author: FullLet2258
replies.body:
I don't really know how to explain it. I'm a huge fan of Vampire Survivors, and that's exactly why I wanted to make something different rather than just replicate it. Both the enemies and abilities are quite different.

I also tried to incorporate some elements from Terraria. For example, halfway through a run, a Crimson Moon event might occur, causing more powerful enemies with higher HP to start spawning. There are also random events inspired by Terraria's nighttime events.

There's even a boss that changes the entire map into a side-scrolling perspective, and your abilities actually change how they work. For example, the grappling hook you see there, which normally pulls enemies towards you, can be used to climb during that phase.

I'm trying to make each run feel a little more unpredictable and give the gameplay its own identity.

replies.author: living_david_aloca
replies.body: It’s completely different but you can’t really say how? It seems like you can be more specific but you just don’t want to spend the time to do so. It’s going to be hard to get people to try your game in that case

replies.author: FullLet2258
replies.body:
Okay, you're right. I didn't explain it very clearly. Here's a more detailed breakdown:, here's how the game actually works:

The game can switch from a top-down perspective to a side-scrolling perspective during special boss encounters.

There are three main game states: Day, Night, and Crimson. Nighttime, rainy nights, and Crimson events can occur randomly during a run.

What makes this interesting is that your abilities behave differently depending on the current game state. In other words, switching perspectives and states actually changes the gameplay. That's one of the reasons I'm spending so much extra time making sure every ability has a different purpose and functionality in each state.

I tried to preserve what I love most about Vampire Survivors: the simple, satisfying gameplay of killing mobs and leveling up.

However, there are also runes, and each rune represents a different ability state. Depending on how you use them, they can even alter enemy behavior.

Bosses also have their own attack patterns. And instead of relying on the usual system where abilities activate automatically, you have direct control over all four of your abilities: the three equipped ones and your character's unique ability.

One important clarification: you don't obtain abilities through the three upgrade choices. You get them by killing enemies and collecting their coins, which you can then use to purchase abilities.

I also tried to make every character feel different to play. For example, the character I'm using here deals a lot of damage, but there's a trade-off: attacking multiple enemies consumes more energy.

I wanted to keep the classic feeling of having several abilities while giving the system my own twist. The three upgrade choices are still there, but they're mainly used to improve your weapons during a run and obtain passive abilities, preserving that classic roguelite progression system.

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: I mean, nice looking but we’ve seen this game 20009 times already. Would love to see some interesting stories or ideas on here.

replies.author: FullLet2258
replies.body:
Don't worry, brother, trust me, it's completely different from most games in the genre. There are passives, runes, abilities that can change states, and even abilities that behave differently depending on what other things you're using.

I tried to combine a lot of elements from games I love, like League of Legends, Terraria, and Vampire Survivors, and bring them all together into one game. Obviously, on a much smaller scale hahaha.

comments.author: PM_Me_Those_
comments.body:
>I haven't spent a single dollar making this game.

Time is money. Every waking second you dedicate to this is money 'spent' in the sense you could have been doing something else. Whether that time spent becomes worth it is really the point. I think saying you haven't spent a single dollar making a game you've worked on for 6+ months is a total lie, though.

replies.author: FullLet2258
replies.body:
Okay, I lied. I actually spent $2 buying an asset pack XD. But I was referring more to AI inference costs. Believe me, brother, I can't afford AI subscriptions (at least for now).

But honestly, I'll take that as a compliment if that's what you meant hahaha. I've really tried to put as much effort as I possibly can into this project.
